sources.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
sources.locator: Complete 7-page paper; §1, equations (3)–(9), PDF pp. 1–2; §2, Lemmas 1–2 and complete proof of the minimax comparison, PDF pp. 2–5; §3 and Table 1, PDF pp. 5–6.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 7-page paper in its full arXiv HTML and PDF versions. Read the full sequence-model and ellipsoid setup, exact cutoff-risk calculation, complete hyperrectangle/product-prior minimax-comparison proof, general-source-to-ellipsoid relation, and all four polynomial/exponential rate rows. The local carriers reproduce complete proofs rather than importing the source proof outline.

contents.name: Gaussian inverse sequence model and weighted ellipsoid setup
contents.support: The local theorem states the positive-noise sequence and ellipsoid hypotheses explicitly and uses the existing exact-risk supplier; it also handles the minimax risk over randomized rules.

contents.name: Exact cutoff risk and first omitted-coordinate maximizer
contents.locator: Lemma 1 and its complete proof, PDF pp. 2–3
contents.support: The exact formula is an earlier batch-8 supplier. The present proof consumes that verified interface and derives the separate minimax lower comparison locally.

contents.name: Minimax comparison over ellipsoids
contents.locator: Theorem, equation (9), and complete proof in §2, PDF pp. 2–5
contents.support: The carrier proves the cutoff upper bound and a local finite-product-prior lower bound. It uses the conservative analytically justified scalar constant sqrt(2e), which still implies the planned factor 2.2.

contents.name: General source sets represented as weighted ellipsoids
contents.support: The carrier proves both inclusions for the real compact-SVD power source ball in the library's |K| convention.

contents.name: Polynomial and exponential axis-rate cases
contents.support: The local corollary redoes all four order balances, including upper and lower cutoff bounds, and does not use the table's displayed cutoff-level constants.

sources.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, draft version December 27, 2011
sources.locator: Complete 446-page manuscript; §2.3, equations (2.26)–(2.30), printed pp. 29–30; §4.3, equation (4.15), printed p. 105; §4.5, Lemma 4.15 and Proposition 4.16, printed pp. 109–110; §4.6, Theorem 4.17 proof, printed pp. 112–113.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched the complete 446-page manuscript, extracted its full text, and read all cited passages. Section 2.3 gives the symmetric two-point posterior and Bayes risk; §4.3 proves the supported-prior lower bound; §4.5 proves product-prior Bayes-risk additivity; and §4.6 gives the scalar projection/minimax comparison. The local proof improves on relying on the numerical 2.22 evaluation by proving a conservative analytic bound.

contents.name: Symmetric two-point prior, posterior mean, posterior variance, and Bayes-risk formula
contents.support: The carrier derives the endpoint-prior posterior and its Bayes risk, then proves an analytic lower bound for the clipped endpoint prior used in each coordinate.

contents.name: A supported prior's Bayes risk lower-bounds minimax risk
contents.support: The carrier checks the inequality directly for its finite product prior before taking the minimax infimum.

contents.name: Product priors make squared-loss Bayes risk additive
contents.support: The carrier locally verifies the finite product likelihood ratio on generating coordinate cylinders and derives the additive posterior-variance lower bound.

contents.name: Projection and minimax risk comparison for a bounded normal mean
contents.locator: §4.6, Theorem 4.17 proof and equations (4.38)–(4.40), printed pp. 112–113
contents.support: The local scalar lemma proves a conservative sqrt(2e) risk factor from the same endpoint-prior formula using an explicit Gaussian-integral inequality.
